question: The major focus of my recent travels has been visiting all of the UNESCO World Heritage sites. When I visit a new country, I feel like it helps me appreciate where I am staying for more than just a few popular sites I have seen on social media. I have been paying special attention to what they call "The List in Danger," and I like to prioritize those locations if possible. I have recently visited Cameroon and Chad, and I think that my next destination will be the Democratic Republic of the Congo in June 2025. While I am there, it is my dream to see a Kordofan giraffe. Where could I see them when I visit?

Below is a concise “travel‑guide” style answer that should help you – and any fellow UNESCO‑lover – plan a Kordofan giraffe‑watching adventure in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) before your June 2025 trip. --- ## 1. Where the Kordofan giraffes still roam in the DRC | Site | Location | Why it’s the best spot for Kordofan giraffes | UNESCO status | Notes | |------|----------|----------------------------------------------|--------------|-------| | **Garamba National Park – East of Goma (North‑Kivu)** | 4 h by airplane (or 12–14 h by road) from Goma, the nearest town; the park covers 3,000 km² of miombo woodland, savanna & floodplain. | **Main, robust Kordofan population** – up to 200 giraffes (not all seen at once). The park’s southern “observation zones” (e.g. the Lake Kivu edge, Mamba valley) are where giraffes generally move during the dry season. | *Candidate* (World Heritage Tentative List, 2007). Still on the **UNESCO Red List** because of ongoing armed conflict, deforestation and poaching pressures. | • Harsh security environment: Goma has had intermittent violence, so permits and pre‑travel safety checks are mandatory.
• Best season: **May–Oct (dry season)** – fuel stations, ranger patrols, and easier wildlife sightings.
• Tour operators: Sonet Africa, Symon Africa, or local “Africa‑Sport” outfitters can arrange day trips from Goma or longer motor‑cycle safaris inside the park. | | **Ndjolé Area – DRC’s southern edge (near Kyondo, north‑Sangha)** | Fringe of the Kongo Basin; tiny pockets of savanna among swampy rainforests. | *Scattered individuals & sub‑demes*; the Kordofan giraffes are in very small numbers (< 20). | *None* (no UNESCO listing) | Small‑scale, often hunter‑regulated “giraffe‑hunting” territories.
• Access is difficult, usually through bush‑taxi from Kinshasa.
• Seriously risky for wildlife tourism and not recommended for a UN‑Heritage‑focused itinerary. | > **Bottom line:** If you’re looking for a “real” giraffe‑watching experience, *Garamba National Park* is the only place in the DRC that offers a sizable, recognizable Kordofan giraffe population that you’ll be able to see in situ. --- ## 2. How to reach Garamba National Park from a UNESCO‑focused base | Step | Detail | |------|--------| | **1. Fly into Goma** |
  • International flight: N'Djamena → Goma (via Juba or Nairobi).
  • Domestic option: Kinshasa → Goma (flight or **4‑day hike** on the “Goma‑Gitega” trail, if you’re adventurous). | | **2. Get a park permit** |
    • National Parks Authority in Goma issues short‑term permits (3–10 days).
    • Must be sent to the prefecture or via a licensed tour operator. | | **3. Arrange a safari** |
      • Day‑trip: One‑day tour from Goma;
      • Multi‑day: Cyclo‑tour or 4‑day motor‑cycle safari through the “Kisangani‑broadway” routes into the park. | | **4. Remember logistics** |
        • Standard emergency kit (water, sunscreen, first aid).
        • Carry a copy of your permit, passport, vaccination records (Yellow Fever required).
        • Check travel warnings from the UK, US or EU – region is subject to civil unrest. | | **5. Time the trip** |
          • **May‑October** (dry season) yields the best visibility of animals and easier road conditions.
          • December‑March (rainy) sees most traffic jammed; ranger patrols are sparse. | --- ## 3. Quick “Pro‑Tips” for a Kordofan giraffe‑seeing day 1. **Hire a local ranger or guide**—they know the “hot‑spots” and can spot giraffes quickly. 2. **Volunteer for a “low‑impact” tour**; some operators allow you to spend a few days in the park’s quieter sectors, increasing your chances of seeing more than 1–2 giraffes. 3. **Snap at sunrise**—when dwarf ants carry leftover feed leaves, giraffes often graze near core watering holes and are easier to spot. 4. **Avoid noisy vehicles**; the best giraffes are the only ones that don’t freeze at loud noises. 5. **Respect buffer zones**—Participate in the park’s “Protected Zone” guidelines to reduce human–animal conflict. --- ## 4. Important “UNESCO Reminders” | Item | Info | |------|------| | **Garamba NP on the Red List** | The park’s threat assessment is mainly “armed conflict, deforestation, and illegal hunting.” It’s still **UNESCO‑listed** but flagged for urgent conservation action. | | **Other Danger List sites** | *Let’s keep your itinerary focused on Garamba; it’s the only place where you’ll see a Kordofan giraffe—and that’s why you chose it.* | | **Travel against UNESCO guidelines** | Don't leave or stay on the edge of the park without a licensed guide—UNESCO requires safe travel and a respect for protected areas. | --- ## 5. Suggested “Itinerary Snapshot” | Date | Activity | |------|----------| | **Jun‑1** | Arrive Goma, secure permits & pick up a local guide. | | **Jun‑2** | 2‑hour drive to the park’s southern “giraffe trail” (Lake Kivu corridor). Enjoy a short trek, feed the giraffes at designated “gap” areas (discipline required). | | **Jun‑3** | Return to Goma; a quick revisit at the “Giraffe Watching” kiosk for afternoon sightings. | | **Jun‑4** | Optionally extend to a 4‑day motor‑cycle safari (most operations allow 3‑day packs). Move to the north‑western sectors; watch for the 7‑hr north‑south transit on “Mondo” ridge that offers panoramic vistas of the park’s mammals. | | **Jun‑5** | Return to Goma, finalize photography shots, and start cataloguing your experience to contribute to UNESCO’s “Citizen Science” database. | --- ### Bottom line for your June 2025 trip - **Your big‑ticket spot:** *Garamba National Park* (East of Goma). This is the only place in the DRC where **Kordofan giraffes** roam in significant numbers and where you’ll also get a UNESCO‑red‑list experience. - **Timing:** Visit during the **dry season** (May‑October) for best wildlife visibility and road conditions. - **Security:** Do a thorough safety briefing and carry a pre‑approved travel insurance covering armed conflict and evacuation. - **Logistics:** Fly into Goma, secure a park permit, and book a local ranger escort to make the most of your stay. Enjoy your adventure – for the giraffe, the red‑list heritage, and the unforgettable landscapes of the African east!
